title: Body Percussion
strapline: Your body is an instrument you always have with you — clap, stamp, pat, click.
intent: Children make music with no equipment at all — clapping, stamping, patting, clicking — always available, always free.
Children find and keep a steady beat and copy rhythmic patterns using their whole bodies.
Children develop coordination, timing and control as they combine sounds and movements.
Children play and perform together, listening, watching a leader and moving as a group.
Children build the sound-and-rhythm vocabulary — beat, clap, stamp, loud, quiet, fast, slow — that music needs.
implementation: Start simple: clap along to a familiar song, keeping the beat steady on each word or pulse.
Play echo games — clap a short pattern for children to copy back, growing longer as they're ready.
Build a body-percussion sequence together: clap, clap, pat knees, stamp — and repeat it as a chant.
Vary loud and quiet, fast and slow, so children control their sounds with intention.
Let children lead — one child claps a pattern for the rest to follow, then hands the lead on.
Weave it into transitions and tidy-up time, so rhythm is part of the day, not a one-off.
Name the sounds and the beat as you go, connecting the movement to the musical words.
key_questions: Can you keep the beat with me?
Can you copy this pattern — clap, clap, stamp?
How can you make a really quiet sound with your body? A loud one?
Can you make up a pattern for us to follow?
Can we do it faster? Slower?

impact.text: Children keep a steady beat with body percussion.
Children copy and create rhythmic patterns.
Children control loud/quiet and fast/slow deliberately.
Children move with coordination and timing.
Children perform together, following a leader and each other.
Children use sound and rhythm vocabulary.

enhancements: Rhythm cards showing clap/stamp/pat symbols to read and perform.
Recorded music of different tempos to keep the beat to.
A 'copy the leader' circle game that passes the lead around.
Songs with built-in actions to layer body percussion onto.
A 'quiet as a mouse, loud as a lion' dynamics game.
Pairing with instruments so some clap while others play.

playing_exploring: Children experiment with the sounds their bodies can make.
They invent new claps, stamps and clicks to try out.
active_learning: Children persist to keep the beat and master a longer pattern.
Leading the group gives them a goal to rise to.
creating_thinking: Children compose their own patterns and sequences.
They decide how to change the sound — louder, faster — for effect.
